note: How each pre-registered prediction is decided. inputs.json is the canonical source of the prediction text; the `text` field below repeats it only so the two can be compared. evaluate.py reads the text from inputs.json by index and refuses to run unless the copy below matches it character for character, so the page cannot restate a prediction in softer words than the one that was committed. The checks themselves were written after the run, against verdicts the evaluator had already computed; that is disclosed in SOURCES.md. Four of the five predictions failed, so there was no flattering direction to write a check toward. One registered prediction contains an arithmetic slip: it names 2023-12-02 as the US reading of 12/02/2024, which is 2024-12-02. inputs.json is frozen, so the text stands as committed and the check scores the prediction against both dates, the generous reading. It failed either way: the model returned 2024-02-12.
